spark.byteSummary:
Understand document, key-value, and wide-column LSM-Tree databases—partition keys, tunable quorums, and access-pattern modeling.

Unlike relational normalization, NoSQL models data around the exact queries your application executes—often denormalizing to keep reads single-partition.

Production NoSQL engineering means avoiding hot partitions, sizing LSM compaction, and combining partition + clustering keys cleanly.

learningJourney.title: Partition keys, sort keys & query-driven modeling
learningJourney.explanation: The Partition Key determines which physical shard owns the row; the Sort/Clustering Key orders rows physically on disk within that partition.

learningJourney.title: LSM-Trees, MemTables, SSTables & Quorum Reads
learningJourney.explanation: Explore how wide-column stores ingest writes sequentially and repair replica drift.

tabbedExplorer.name: LSM Write Path
tabbedExplorer.title: Commit Log + MemTable → Immutable SSTables
tabbedExplorer.desc: Writes append to a commit log and update an in-memory skip-list (MemTable), flushing sorted SSTables sequentially to disk.
tabbedExplorer.rule: Bloom filters on every SSTable prevent unnecessary disk seeks on missing keys.
tabbedExplorer.use: Write-heavy telemetry, messaging, IoT, activity feeds.

tabbedExplorer.name: Tunable Quorum
tabbedExplorer.title: W + R > N Strong Read Consistency
tabbedExplorer.desc: With N=3 replicas, setting W=2 and R=2 guarantees every read overlaps at least one up-to-date write replica.
tabbedExplorer.rule: Reads still require Read Repair / Hinted Handoff / Merkle Anti-Entropy to converge lagging nodes.

learningJourney.title: Hot partitions, tombstones & unbounded partitions
learningJourney.explanation: Design keys and TTLs so partitions stay bounded and tombstones don't tank read latency.

qaDetails.summary: Why do heavy DELETEs slow down reads in Cassandra/ScyllaDB?
qaDetails.body: Deletes write Tombstone markers in LSM-trees instead of erasing old SSTable entries immediately. Range scans must read and skip thousands of tombstones until compaction purges them.

qaDetails.summary: How do you prevent a hot partition when one key gets 80% of traffic?
qaDetails.body: Add a random write-sharding suffix (`KEY#{0..9}`) or time-bucket the partition key (`USER#42#2026-11`).

knowledgeCheck.question: In a replicated NoSQL store with N=3 replicas, which quorum setting guarantees overlap between writes and reads?

options.feedback: 1 + 1 = 2 <= 3, so a read can hit two stale replicas.
Correct! Since W + R = 4 > 3, at least one replica in the read quorum holds the latest write.

tipsAndTricks: Design your partition key around your highest-QPS queries—never pick a low-cardinality boolean or status field as a partition key.
Avoid unbounded partitions (e.g., all events for one customer forever); bucket by time (`tenant#2026-11`).
Prefer TTL expiration or partition drops over massive point-delete storms in LSM-tree databases to avoid tombstone buildup.
finalSummaryEyebrow: The idea to keep with you
finalSummaryTitle: Model around queries, pick high-cardinality partition keys, and design for eventual consistency.
finalSummary: Production NoSQL engineering means avoiding hot partitions, sizing LSM compaction, and combining partition + clustering keys cleanly.
